# Button

The primary action trigger — a text button with optional leading and trailing icons, in six styles. Light and dark are handled automatically by page-level modes, so you choose a style, not a theme.

## Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA: `1.4.3`, `1.4.11`, `2.1.1`, `2.4.7`, `2.5.8`, `4.1.2`

- Renders a native <button>, or an <a> when it navigates — never a div with a click handler.
- The label is the accessible name; an icon-only button needs an aria-label.
- Focus is visible on the control itself (2.4.7) and the target is at least 24x24 (2.5.8).
- Disabled is conveyed to assistive tech, not by colour alone (1.4.1).
- Give it an accessible name. The Label provides it; for an icon-only button, set an aria-label. WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value.
- Real button semantics. Render as <button> (or <a> when it navigates via href). Tab to focus, Enter / Space to activate. WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard.
- Ship the focus ring. The focus state's ring must exist in code so keyboard focus stays visible. WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible.
- Mind contrast on inverse styles. On media or colored surfaces keep the label and icons at 4.5:1 (text) / 3:1 (UI) against the background — add a scrim if needed. WCAG 1.4.3 & 1.4.11.
- Target size at least 24x24px (44x44 on touch). WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum).
- disabled is communicated, not just dimmed — remove it from the tab order and expose the state to assistive tech.
